name: Holt & Rein Melton Overcoat
description:
A knee-length overcoat in midnight navy boiled wool melton, structured and clean-lined with a hidden placket, welt pockets, and a back vent that sits perfectly flat. Holt & Rein is a Tier 4 heritage label — not flashy, not technological, just extraordinarily well-made traditional tailoring. The shoulders are canvas-padded, the chest is half-lined in silk-analogue charmeuse, and the collar rolls with a softness that takes a skilled block-presser to achieve. Every coat is cut by hand in their Spire-adjacent atelier.

This is the coat of senior analysts, mid-level corponation liaisons, and the kind of Tier 3 professional who saved up for something that will outlast their career. It communicates seriousness without aggression, authority without ostentation. On the street, it reads as expensive to anyone who knows fabric. To those who don't, it just reads as correct.
what_it_says: You have good taste and the patience to find it. You are not someone who needs to announce themselves.
story_hooks: A Holt & Rein overcoat left at a crime scene belongs to a registered identity that doesn't match any living person — the coat is three years old but the identity was created six months ago.
The label inside all Holt & Rein coats contains a serial number traceable to the specific tailor who cut it — someone is using this to track a person they believe is still alive.
A Tier 2 character inherits one of these coats from a dead relative and finds that wearing it opens doors — people assume they belong in rooms they've never entered before.
